doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later Blue Note years and ending the habit
title: Blue Note reissues and who owns his music
summary: Blue Note issues unreleased sessions without asking him, and catalogs get sold on to firms like Coca Cola.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: What’s your feeling about things that weren’t released originally, that then they – Blue Note – brings out later? Did you participate in any of that? Did they ask you, “Do you want to put this session out?”?

No, man, they don’t ask you nothing. They don’t even send you a record. They don’t even send you a CD in the mail and say, “Thanks a lot. We’re letting this out.” You just hear somebody say, “Hey, man, I just picked up a new CD by you called” whatever.
Vertigo. They’re making these compilations of different albums, mixing and matching. They’re going to be doing that forever. That’s what they do.
So you don’t – that’s not acceptable to you? Or you’re not happy?
There’s nothing I can do about it.

It has to be acceptable, because that’s what it is. I don’t like it. I’d much rather be making money like they make money. They’re making money for their families, their grandchildren, their great-grand – that’s what they’re doing.
I look at catalogs like an oil well. They just keep pumping.

Yeah, they keep pumping it out and selling whole batches of music to other companies. Some of my music is owned by Coca Cola and Company and all that kind of stuff. So you don’t know where your music ends up. It may be called such – Ajax Music Company, but that could – behind that could be RCA Victor or any number of things, Coca Cola or whatever.
